newsitem.title: USA: Austria says will not change view on IMF gold.
newsitem.headline: Austria says will not change view on IMF gold.

text.p: Austria remains opposed to sales of gold by the International Monetary Fund and has no intention of changing its view any time soon, Austrian Finance Minister Viktor Klima said on Monday.

Klima told a briefing on the sidelines of the annual meeting of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank that he expected a core group of countries which opposed the gold sale plan to continue to hold this view long-term.
"We assume that Switzerland, Germany and Austria will be consistent in sticking to their view," he said.

A small core of European countries, spearheaded by Germany, has so far successfully fought off plans by a majority of IMF nations to sell off a small amount of the Fund's gold to stop a financing gap.
They have argued that the gold sales are not absolutely essential at the moment and could set a bad precedent.

The issue has temporarily been taken off the agenda, with the 85 percent majority support for the sales seemingly lacking. Supporters of the plan have had to content themselves with assurances that the IMF will get the funding it needs.

Klima said Austria's objections to the sales were two-fold. "Firstly we are worried that if IMF's substance is used to fund running business this could trigger further demands in the future," Klima said.
"Secondly, we believe that large countries with a lot of influence at the IMF should fulfil their bilateral obligations," he added, in a thinly-veiled reference to the United States.
Problems in gaining Congressional support for various aid funding means that the United States has fallen back in some of its international obligations.
